## TL;DR

The Work board's search and quick filters were only half wired. The phone queue
keeps them in the URL, so they survive a reload. At 720 px and up the desktop
board ignored those URL filters and gave no sign that tasks were hidden. The
board now applies the same predicate as the queue, shows the active filters in
a chip bar, and offers a Clear filters control that removes only the queue
keys. Round 2 closes the review items: the chip bar also appears on the pipeline
view with a note that it doesn't filter, unusable URL values show as ignored
chips, Clear keeps every non-filter query entry, and the remaining gaps are
filed as follow-up tasks.

## Work and rationale

The search, quick filters and Reset control live in `MobileWorkQueue.vue` and
write to the URL (#1138). The desktop board kept its own sort and visibility
toggles in global localStorage keys, and its status filter was a `?status=`
key. Phone widths render the queue below 720 px, and 768 and 1280 px render the
board. The board silently dropped the queue's URL filters, which was the defect.

Changes:

- `src/ui-app/src/lib/workQueueFilters.ts` holds the filter type, the reader,
  the predicate (moved from the queue unchanged), the chip list, the ignored-value
  notices, and the clear helper.
- `MobileWorkQueue.vue` calls the shared predicate. Its behavior is unchanged.
- `BoardQueueFilters.vue` renders the chips, the ignored chips (dashed), the
  pipeline note when `applied` is false, and Clear filters.
- `WorkView.vue` applies the filters in `visibleByStatus`, so columns, counts and
  keyboard navigation agree. The bar shows on the board and on the pipeline view.
  Clear calls `router.replace` with the query minus the queue keys.

Round 2 decisions: the pipeline view keeps showing the bar and says plainly that
it doesn't filter, rather than hiding the filters. An unusable `priority` or
`mine` value gets a notice chip instead of being dropped, and Clear removes it.
`clearWorkQueueFilterQuery` now removes only the five keys and keeps null and
repeated values, which the old version dropped.

Tests (all passing, none skipped): 19 browser-suite cases, which are 8 jsdom
behavior cases plus WebKit fit checks at 375, 768 and 1280 px for the chip bar,
the pipeline note and an ignored chip. The pure-logic suite has 6 cases.

Follow-ups filed: #1259 (a search input on the desktop board) and #1260 (queue
sort and mobile-only status values on the board).

## Approaches tried

A search input on the desktop board would add a new control at wide widths,
which the task didn't ask for. Applying and showing the URL filters was the
smaller change, and the input is now a tracked follow-up.

For the reload race where a late `router.replace` could overwrite a keystroke,
I reasoned that a later replace supersedes an earlier one. I did not test it
because jsdom doesn't reproduce it. The QA record lists it as uncovered.

## Challenges and blockers

The scoped check failed in `board-column-labels.test.ts`, a DashboardView block,
after my change. I bisected it. A bare read of `route.query` inside
`visibleByStatus` reproduced it, and skipping the WorkView block made it pass.
The cause was three WorkView mounts that were never unmounted. They stayed live
and broke the next DashboardView mount. The app unmounts WorkView on navigation,
so this is a test-isolation defect. I added the missing `unmount()` calls.

The WebKit tests need `dist/ui` built first, which `bun run build:ui` provides.
Review shots are declared on desktop routes only, since the capture width is
chosen by the harness. Touch behavior on a real device is not covered and needs
a human.

## Key learnings

Search state that lives in a narrow-screen component is invisible to the rest of
the app. Reading the URL keys where the board renders fixed it, without
duplicating state. Moving the predicate into a shared module kept the queue and
the board in agreement by construction.

A silent drop, whether a filter the view doesn't apply or a value the reader
can't use, is the actual bug class here. Showing an explicit chip or note for
every case is cheaper to verify than trying to prove nothing was dropped.
